code.layout: cats 0..d-1, ancillas d..2d-2; stabilizer j = X_j X_{j+1}; CX(ancilla j -> cat j) then (-> cat j+1)

noise_model.name: kerrcat(nbar=1, kappa/K=0.000167, n_th=0.08, K=10 MHz, LRU=True)

provenance.preset: presets/kerrcat.yaml (the DA21 tables and every other literature number with its source)
provenance.cycle: DA21 Tables I-II operation times (units of 1/K): T_P 16.5 / 2.6, T_M = T_P + T_CD 58.5 / 5.1 at |a|^2 = 1 / 6.25 (log-linear in |a|^2 between, 6.25 values beyond), T_CX = 115/|a|^2 (112.6 / 18.47); K/2pi = 10.0 MHz -> round 4854 ns
provenance.cx_channel[Z]: DA21 Tables I-II: CX infidelity x bias/(1 + bias) (power law in kappa/K, log-linear in |a|^2 between 1 and 6.25, constant beyond since T_CX ~ 1/|a|^2), times (1 + 2 n_th)/(1 + 2 x 0.08) for other thermal populations; split Z_aI : IZ_d : Z_aZ_d = 1 : 1/2 : 1/2 (DA21 generic bias-preserving CX, pp. 8-9). Our loss-and-gain estimate 2 kappa (1 + 2 n_th) |a|^2 T_CX agrees within 5% at |a|^2 = 6.25 and 5-12% at 1
provenance.cx_channel[non-Z]: DA21 Tables I-II: CX infidelity/(1 + bias), split equally over the 12 bit-flip-type Paulis (no published split); beyond |a|^2 = 6.25 heating-limited, scaled by 6.25/|a|^2 (our estimate kappa n_th T_CX/2 = 1.2e-4 accounts for 84% of the DA21 value 1.5e-4 at the design point)
provenance.p_data[Z]: kappa (1 + 2 n_th) |a|^2 per unit time during T_P + T_M, and during the other CX layer for the two boundary cats (PU20 Table I, thermal bath)
provenance.p_data[X]: heating-limited bit-flip plateau T_X = (kappa n_th)^-1 over the same idle times (Frattini et al., PRX 14, 031040 (2024), plateau model; measured T_X ~ 0.6-1.2 ms: Hajr et al., PRX 14, 041049 (2024); Qing et al., PNAS 123, e2520479123 (2026))
provenance.p_prep/p_meas: DA21 Tables I-II preparation (Z + Y) and measurement infidelity (same interpolation as the CX); at the design point 0.003 and 0.008
provenance.p_data_meas_z: well (Z) readout: single-shot infidelity 0.46% (Frattini et al., PRX 14, 031040 (2024))
provenance.leak_data: single-photon gain excites the first excited manifold at kappa n_th (PU20 p. 7); per round kappa n_th T_round (DA21: 1e-4 - 1e-3 per qubit and round); return by loss kappa (1 + n_th) and, with the LRU, by two-photon loss 4 kappa2 |a|^2 during the kappa2 half of each CX (DA21 two-step CX, kappa2 = K/10); return by two-photon loss gives a phase flip (PU20), so the return re-randomizes Z only; while leaked the neighbouring syndromes are random (incoherent approximation, Marshall & Kafri 2025)
provenance.leak_anc: ancillas are Kerr cats too: the same rates; a leaked ancilla gives a random outcome; its effect on the CX partners is not modelled
provenance.note: DA21 publish only infidelity and average bias, and neglect the residual leakage in their code simulations; current experiments (K/2pi = 1.2 MHz, T1 ~ 40 us, n_th 4-5%: Hajr et al., Qing et al.) are far above the repetition-code threshold with this CX
provenance.validation: reproduces the DA21 CX, preparation and measurement numbers by construction; compared with the DA21 exact n = 9 repetition-code simulation in examples/literature_checks_models.py

generator.sampler: stim.FlipSimulator + leakage in the incoherent approximation (dem/noise_models.py)

layout.heralds: round-major; per round the d-1 syndrome-erasure heralds of ancillas 0..d-2 (kind 1: ancilla found outside the qubit subspace, outcome random), then, if the model has them, the heralded bit flips of cats 0..d-1 (kind 2); the same bits are the herald detectors of detectors.b8, coordinates (x, round, kind); kind 0 = syndrome detectors
layout.leakage: rounds x (cats then ancillas) (round-major); 1 = leaked during that round

baseline_decoding.decoder: X basis: PyMatching 2 on the circuit DEM (leakage not in the DEM), correlated matching with the heralds; Z basis: none (no Z stabilizers), heralded cat bit flips undone
baseline_decoding.note: Z basis: the failure is the odd-parity probability of all cats, including the initial and final well readout
